subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should core permanently support a dedicated opt-in deferred-maintenance timeout and synchronous queue timeout hook even though the plugin's maintain operation may continue after the host releases the lane?
rationale: Source and proof support the implementation, but code review cannot choose the permanent config surface, shared queue API, or acceptable plugin-abandonment semantics without owner intent.

options.title: Approve the opt-in contract
options.body: Keep the dedicated setting and host-side fence/checkpoint, explicitly documenting that plugin-owned work may continue after timeout.

options.title: Reuse the compaction safety budget
options.body: Remove the extra setting and bind maintenance to the existing host timeout, accepting the broader default behavior and upgrade implications.

options.title: Require cooperative cancellation
options.body: Pause this PR until the context-engine contract defines cancellation or another owner-controlled way to stop timed-out plugin work.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Keep the dedicated setting and host-side fence/checkpoint, explicitly documenting that plugin-owned work may continue after timeout.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available current-main history signal for closely related same-session transcript ordering and settlement behavior, although final product authority is not established by this evidence.
